To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the On-Surface radiation Condition method has been developed for the numerical representation acoustic scattering in the frequency domain, and that it has been applied to various model problems and to a few important practical applications.

the On-Surface Radiations Condition is a powerful and efficient method to model acoustic scattering problems in complex environments; it can be implemented on standard finite element meshes; it is well suited for the solution of exterior problems and penetrable scatterer problems; it can be used to improve the convergence of the iterative solution of the Helmholtz equation and it can be used for the modelling of large scale scattering problems in complex geometries at high frequencies

the OSRC method has proven to be very efficient for solving acoustic scattering problems, that it is very flexible in terms of the type of boundary condition it can handle and that the OSRC approach is a promising alternative to classical integral equations methods in view of a future fast iterative solution of large scale scattering problems in the high frequency regime.

the development of efficient numerical methods for acoustic scattering problems.
the development of efficient and accurate computational methods for the solution of exterior acoustic scattering problems in 3D.
the development of new numerical methods for the simulation of acoustic wave scattering problems in exterior domains.

the On-Surface-Radiation Condition Method is a promising and efficient tool for numerical simulation of scattering problems in the high frequency regime, but that it is not yet a mature method and that many improvements are still possible and necessary.
the OSRC method is a promising tool for solving a large class of acoustic scattering problems at high frequencies.
the OSRC method is an extremely powerful and promising numerical tool for solving a large class of problems arising in acoustic scattering.

the On-Surface Radiating Condition method is now well understood and is a very powerful tool for solving a wide class of acoustic scattering problems.
the OSRC method is a very powerful tool for the numerical representation and solution of scattering problems in acoustics, but also in other wave propagation problems.

the OSRC method is a very promising tool for solving large scale problems at high frequency and that the recent developments are paving the way to its practical use.
